# Level-of-detail texture mapping

Also called: Level-of-Detail Texture Blocks, Low-resolution texture blocks, Raster-based LOD texture

## Overview
Level-of-detail texture mapping reduces fragment shader load by rasterizing lower-resolution texture blocks whenever local volume detail or projected resolution allows [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

## How it works
Inputs: 3D volume dataset, camera parameters, and a criterion for projected resolution or local detail [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
Outputs: Rendered image with optimized fragment shader execution [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

Data structures: Texture blocks representing sub-volumes at varying resolutions [S1, unofficial][S2, book]. LOD selection criteria based on projected size or local detail [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

Numbered steps:
1. Evaluate the projected size of volume elements or local detail for the current camera view [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
2. Identify regions where projected resolution or local detail permits lower sampling [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
3. Select lower-resolution texture blocks for those regions [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
4. Rasterize the selected blocks, reducing fragment shader invocations per unit area [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
5. Composite fragments to produce the final image [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

## Subtopics

### Texture Box Approximation
An alternative approach by Li and Kaufman that approximates the object by a set of texture boxes, efficiently clipping empty space from rasterization [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

## Operating characteristics
Time and memory complexity: Reduces fragment shader load compared to brute-force rendering [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
Scaling: Not given in the sources.
Strengths: Reduces computational load on fragment shaders [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
Limitations: Not given in the sources.
When to use: When fragment shader load is a bottleneck [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
When not: When hardware supports efficient brute-force rendering [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

## Background
Origin: Developed to reduce the load for fragment shaders on volume rendering hardware such as the VolumePro500 and VolumePro 1000 [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
History: Research efforts concentrated on reducing fragment shader load by devising level-of-detail methods [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
Usage: Used in volume rendering on commodity graphics hardware [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
